reviews.x: I had to get my feet beach ready over night and got this tool. My heels get really calloused from all that "barefoot" training/running stuff. I bought the coarse rollers and used that first. It's messy- take it outdoors or in the bath. If you have borderline OCD like me, reign that madness in, otherwise you're going to take off too much and your feet will be tender. Do over a few days and still use a good moisturizer on your heels. reviews.t: Personal Hygiene
reviews.x: This is an excellent product.  It has much more power than the earlier models.  I think the rechargeable unit was an improvement over the battery operated.

reviews.t: Emjoi Micro-Pedi Pro Foot Buffer Rechargeable.
reviews.x: I love this product. It performs exactly as advertised. I have used it 4 times so far without needing to recharge. These uses were not just for a moment or two either, but for a considerable time. There are many complaints of dust everywhere. If held properly, with the handle downward, and a trash can under your fee, the movement of air from the rotation of the buffer will push the dust out vents on the back of the micro-pedi into the trash can or other receptacle. If you hold it upside down...

reviews.t: Rechargeable Micro-Pedi Pro is fantastic
reviews.x: I must really love this tool.  I bought myself one and liked it so much that I ordered two more for other people.  I really like the fact that it is rechargeable and I don't have to keep buying batteries.  It does a smooth job on my rough feet.  I don't even have to get pedicures anymore.

reviews.t: Fine for sanding light calluses. Poor for removing heavy calluses
reviews.x: If you have calluses that are a few millimeters in thickness that just need to be made smooth, the Emjoi may be the perfect solution for you. However, if you have serious calluses that actually need removal, rather than just minor shaping, you will find the Emjoi to be very, very slow, about 10 times slower than the product I eventually replaced it with, the Microplane foot rasp.  The Emjoi works by literally sanding the skin, something that requires the skin be dry at the time, and therein lies

reviews.t: The battery is good for about 30 minutes
reviews.x: We have been using this product for six months  - it works!  We feel the rechargeable unit is over priced.  The battery is good for about 30 minutes.  The electronics are poor as you do not know the battery status or when the unit is recharged.  Recharging takes many hours and you don't know when it is fully charged.  We would not purchase this product again but would consider the plug in unit.  The pads are holding up much better than we expected lasting very well.  It does an excellent job rem

reviews.t: Best thing invented since sliced bread
reviews.x: It is wonderful.  No cutting at all, just a nice little pummace stone that gently smooths the feet.  You will love it, every woman I know who has one, loves it.  Now they are making stronger ones for men.  This just keeps getting better and better.

reviews.t: Corded vs. Cordless Review
reviews.x: We wore out our battery operated Emjoi after 3 years. NO, You cannot use it at all if batteries are dead and you plug it into the wall socket, at least ours doesn't. Secondly, you cannot take out the batteries and put in fresh ones. You must plug into the wall socket and wait a couple of hours. The averag

reviews.t: Ineffective product!
reviews.x: Inspired by excellent reviwes, i purchased this marvelous device, hoping that it would help me to cope with callous skin on my feet. It was a dissapointment. In general Emoji works, and the roller rotates, but the power is so low, that it is just not able to remove the dry skin from feet. And when to push it a little bit harder- it just stops. This product is ineffective, so don't hope that it will help you to get off callous, and dont waste your money.

reviews.t: Good power, would recommend but a few small changes would make the Micro-Pedi even better
reviews.x: So far, I'm pretty pleased with this buffer, but there are a few small things that I think Emjoi could improve on. I was able to use this buffer for both feet after only charging for 30 minutes, then plugged it in for the recommended time. It would be nice if the red light ever went off to let you know when it was charged, but this hasn't been an issue since it's always charged when I need it. The directions are silent about leaving the product on the charger--I read the instructions carefuilly, and most products allow leaving them on the charger.  The second time I tried using this Emjoi, Micro-Pedi, it ran for less than 15 seconds and then stopped.  It would occasionally work for a few seconds but never more than 15 seconds before it would stop

reviews.t: Emjoy waiting for seller to respond.
reviews.x: I used the Emjoy and liked it but it will not recharge. I am waiting for the seller to respond. So far everyone with the battery Enjoy is.  Happy.

reviews.t: Really works, but too bad the rollers don't last longer
reviews.x: The Micro-Pedi buffer works just fine for me.  I've had it for a month now and haven't had to recharge it yet.  It has quite a bit of power and speed, and does a great job on my heels.  I've never experienced it stopping when I put pressure on it as some have reported here.  Only negative is the refill rollers don't last as long as I'd like.  I'm squeezing 3-4 uses out of each, but they're most effective with the first two uses.  Unfortunately, the rollers are pretty pricey--I'm hoping some vend

reviews.t: Wow--this thing really works!
reviews.x: The Emjoi Micro-Pedi does everything it says it will:  if your heels are super-dry, it might take a while to get them to baby-softness, but after the initial use, all you have to do to maintain is to use the device every several days, and just a few passes over each heel should do it.  I have used it numerous times since I bought it and still have not had to replace the original head. Highly recommended!

reviews.t: Great little gadget to keep your feet smooth
reviews.x: I love the Emjoi pedi foot buffer.  It works well if you use it every few days. If the rollers look worn out after a use or two, they aren't - just rinse them off and the color is back.  What you were seeing was dead skin.  I highly recommend this product; a good deal for the price.  I use it every other day and my feet are always smooth.

reviews.t: Very expensive and not as good as the much cheaper alternative.
reviews.x: This thing is pretty much as advertised, but it's not worth the money. There are readily available manual removers for dead skin that work better and cost much, much less. Any pharmacy department will have them. Too, the manual ones do not consume replacement parts. If you don't break it, you've got it for life.

reviews.t: I highly recommend....
reviews.x: I highly recommend the rechargeable Micro-Pedi. I bought my first one about 4 years ago and love it. I use it about every other day and it has dramatically improved my dry heels and calluses. Recently I noticed it wasn't working as well as it used to and the battery wasn't holding a charge as long as it used to. reviews.t: Wow! It's like having new feet!

I've been dealing with callouses on my feet since I was a teenager in the 70s wearing platform heels. In my twenties, I used to cut them off with scissors. reviews.t: Use as directed
reviews.x: Although this buffer works good, I would suggest it be used on maintained callouses. The rollers get hot on thick, hard callouses when constant firm pressure is applied..(not suggested)..use cautiously if you have little sensation on your feet.. The vender is amazing! My first buffer did not work, wouldn't even charge. The vender was very helpful in replacing the unit for the one I have now (which works just fine..)

claims.text: Many reviewers love the product and say it effectively smooths rough, calloused feet, with several buying extra units for others.
The rechargeable version is widely praised over battery-operated models, though some find it overpriced and note the battery lasts only about 30 minutes with no status indicator.
Some reviewers find it too weak or slow for heavy calluses, working better on light calluses.
The device creates dust/mess during use, which reviewers suggest managing by holding it properly or using it outdoors.
A few reviewers report charging or battery issues, including not being able to use it while plugged in with dead batteries.
